testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a low air pressure warning light. This light is red and may have a buzzer sound with it.

questions.question: The most common type of foundation brake used is the:
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: If you plan to slow down, you can warn drivers behind you by:

options.text: Tapping the brakes a few times before braking.
Turning on one set of turn signals.
Putting your hand out the driver's side window and waving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tapping the brakes a few times before braking.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times before slowing down. This flashes your brake lights and warns drivers behind you that you are about to slow down.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks:

options.text: Usually have low centers of gravity.
Usually have high centers of gravity.
Usually are not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and need special care when driving. The materials inside can shift during travel, which changes how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: To help your vehicle be seen by others:

options.text: Your headlights should be turned off during the day.
Your headlights should be covered with grease.
Your headlights should be used, but only in the rain.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlights clean. Clean lights give off more light and help other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks require special care because:

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity. Their loads also shift during travel. Be extra careful when turning and taking curves.

questions.question: On trucks and buses, where are ABS malfunction lamps located?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Steer with one hand to keep the other hand free.

questions.explanation: Follow posted speed limits in work zones. Slow down if road or weather conditions are poor. Slow down even more if workers are near the roadway.

questions.question: When starting the engine of a truck with a trailer, how can you tell if the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer will stay on.
The red light on the trailer will flash three times and then stay on.
All the rear lights on the trailer will flash and then shut off.
The blue light near the driver's door will light.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer will stay on.
questions.explanation: Trailers with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have a yellow malfunction lamp on the left rear. If this light stays on after starting the engine, the ABS is not working.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Cancel your signal once your turn or lane change is complete.
Don't signal unless another vehicle is close.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't signal unless another vehicle is close.
questions.explanation: Always signal before a turn or lane change. Start signaling early and keep the signal on during the turn. Turn off your signal after the turn or lane change is complete.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, like at dawn or dusk, how do you make your vehicle more visible?
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor (dawn, dusk, rain, or snow), turn on your low beam headlights. This makes your vehicle easier to see. Do not use high beams when driving near other vehicles.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS stops working?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) works with your regular brakes. If ABS fails, your basic brakes still work. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for assistance.
Continue trying to remove the vehicle from the tracks.
Walk down the tracks to look for an oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for assistance.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, immediately exit the vehicle and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services right away.

questions.question: Who is allowed to drive a vehicle that requires hazardous materials placards?

options.text: A driver with a hazardous materials endorsement
A driver with a minimum of 10 years of commercial driving experience
Any person who thinks they can

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: What does blocking a load do?

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done.
Can only be done in dry weather.

questions.explanation: Blocking cargo prevents it from sliding during transport. When cargo shifts, it makes steering and handling harder for the driver.

questions.question: Can you use tires of different sizes on a vehicle?

options.text: May be used on a tractor.
May be used on a trailer.
Should be used in adverse weather conditions.
Should not be used on a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used on a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Tires of different sizes should not be used on a vehicle. This is a problem that must be fixed during a vehicle inspection.

questions.question: Which situation may result in being denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: The TSA considers you a security threat.
You are a lawful U.S. citizen.
You work for a foreign company.
You do not have perfect vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: The TSA considers you a security threat.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if: you renounce U.S. citizenship; you are not a lawful permanent resident; you are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies; you are judged mentally defective or committed to a mental institution; or the TSA considers you a security threat.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice may look wet. Be careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, what may need to happen?

options.text: The vehicle should be parked uphill.
The vehicle should be parked downhill.
The engine may have to be left running.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine may have to be left running.
questions.explanation: On some vehicles, you may need to leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
The total weight of a vehicle before cargo
The maximum weight allowed to be transported by a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle plus all of its cargo.

questions.question: Drivers may use ____ red reflective warning triangles when their vehicle is stopped on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Place three red reflective triangles around your vehicle when it is stopped on the road. This warns other drivers.

questions.question: When taking the basic control skills test, drivers are:

options.text: Not permitted to stop and exit the vehicle to look at the vehicle's position.
Encouraged not to exit the vehicle to look at the vehicle's position.
Allowed to leave the vehicle, but only if the vehicle is placed in reverse.
Allowed to leave the vehicle, but only if the vehicle is placed in neutral and the parking brake is set.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed to leave the vehicle, but only if the vehicle is placed in neutral and the parking brake is set.
questions.explanation: You can exit the vehicle to check its position during the basic control skills test. First, put the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake. You can check the position twice, except during straight line backing when you can check it only once.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle, the oil pressure should:

options.text: Slowly build up pressure over a few minutes.
Come up to a normal level within a few seconds.
Start high, then decrease quickly while the engine runs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come up to a normal level within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds. Do not drive if the oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles transporting hazardous materials.
Can help a driver see a large area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help a driver see a large area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved and let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects in convex mirrors look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When testing a parking brake, the vehicle should:

options.text: Be placed in a low gear while the driver attempts to pull forward.
Be inspected by a professional mechanic.
Be driven while the parking brake is applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be placed in a low gear while the driver attempts to pull forward.
questions.explanation: To test the parking brake: fasten your seatbelt, set the parking brake, release the trailer brake if needed, put the vehicle in low gear, and try to pull forward. If the parking brake does not hold, it needs repair.

questions.question: Retreaded tires:

options.text: May be used on the front axle of a school bus.
May be used on the rear axles of a school bus.
Cannot be used on a school bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be used on the rear axles of a school bus.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus. They may only be used on the rear axles.

questions.question: When parked on the side of a road, you should:

options.text: Stand in the roadway and wave your arms.

questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. This alerts other drivers to your vehicle. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: Cargo on flatbed trailers should be:
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers and open trailers must be securely tied down. This prevents it from shifting or falling off during transport.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts in the engine compartment should be:

options.text: Inspected only if they seem frayed.

questions.explanation: Check all belts in the engine compartment for tightness and wear during your pre-trip inspection.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which braking system?
questions.explanation: The service brake system uses the brake pedal. You press it to apply and release the brakes while driving normally.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, press down on the brake pedal.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance will be ____ times longer.
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, your braking distance becomes four times longer. A crash at the higher speed will also be four times more powerful.

questions.question: What can change a vehicle's height?
questions.explanation: Heavy weight lowers a vehicle. A vehicle sits higher when empty and lower when loaded. A vehicle that fits under an overpass when fully loaded may not fit when empty.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should you do?

options.text: Wave your arms at other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire failure can cause you to lose control. Unless you are about to hit something, stay off the brake until your vehicle slows down.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, what should you remember?

options.text: You can usually outrun a train.
Do not rely only on warning signals.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Only check the track closest to your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals.
questions.explanation: Never trust warning signals alone. Never try to race a train across the crossing. If there are multiple tracks, check all tracks in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: Which is not a problem when inspecting your vehicle's exhaust system?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts

questions.explanation: Problems to look for include loose, broken, or missing pipes and mufflers; loose or missing brackets and bolts; exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts or tires; and leaking exhaust parts.

questions.question: A cardboard box in the road could be dangerous because:

options.text: You should drive off the road to avoid it.
It could contain something hard that damages your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It could contain something hard that damages your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is a potential hazard. Even something that looks harmless, like a cardboard box, could contain hard or heavy objects that damage your vehicle.

questions.question: Which is not a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Brake pads with oil or grease on them
Brake pads clean and free of oil or grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake pads clean and free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: Signs of brake problems include cracked drums; pads or shoes with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them; and pads that are missing, broken, or dangerously thin.

questions.question: When must you sign a written vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Only if defects were found and repairs have been certified
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000
Only if a police officer asks you to

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects were found and repairs have been certified
questions.explanation: You must sign the vehicle inspection report only if defects were noted and certified as either repaired or not requiring repair.

questions.question: When pulled over on the side of the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Always turn on your emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. This warns other drivers. It is especially important at night.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: ABS malfunction lamps are yellow.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether your vehicle fits under a bridge, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Slow down and find an alternate route if you cannot tell whether your vehicle will fit under a bridge or overhead object.

questions.question: When exiting a bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.

questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and hold the handrail at all times when exiting. Exiting incorrectly will result in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a header board, it should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: The header board must be secure, undamaged, and strong enough to contain cargo.

questions.question: Before looking under your vehicle's hood during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Set the parking brake and/or use chock blocks.
Leave the vehicle in a low gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set the parking brake and/or use chock blocks.
questions.explanation: Set the parking brake and properly chock the wheels before inspecting under the hood.

questions.question: Cargo on a flatbed or open trailer must be:

options.text: Loose so it can shift when turning.
Heavy enough that it won't move.

questions.explanation: Cargo must be securely tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling off during travel.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is thin and clear enough that you can see the road through it. It makes the road look wet.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off fog and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, which of the following should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Find an escape route like an escape ramp or side street. Do not accelerate.

questions.question: A cargo cover that flaps while the vehicle is moving:

options.text: Allows air flow to keep cargo cool.

questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap in the wind. A flapping cover can tear loose and expose cargo or block your view and others' view.
